newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco, India invest $230 mln in phosphate industry.
newsitem.headline: Morocco, India invest $230 mln in phosphate industry.

text.p: Morocco's state-run Office Cherifien des Phosphates (OCP) and India's Chambal Fertilisers and Chemicals Ltd on Wednesday signed a $230 million accord to set up a joint-venture firm to produce phosphate by-products.

Mourad Cherif, head of the OCP told a news conference on Wednesday evening: "The Moroccan-Indian joint venture firm (50/50) is expected to produce 1.0 million tonnes of sulphuric acid and 330,000 tonnes of phosphoric acid annually."
The two parties will invest a total of $230 million in the project which will be located in Jorf Lasfar industrial complex, near El-Jadida city on the Atlantic coast, Cherif said.
The plant is expected to be operational in 1999 and 2/3 of its output will be devoted to Chambal, he said.
"Phosphoric acid trade on the World market represents an estimated 3.4 million tonnes of which India imports 50 percent annually," Cherif told reporters.
Morocco is the first world exporter of phosphoric acid with an average 1.7 million tonne per year or nearly 50 percent of the international market stake, he added.
Morocco's main employer with 28,000 workers, OCP earlier said it plans to invest $1.05 billion over the next five years to upgrade its existing facilities and expand output capacities.

Chambal, which is a subsidiary of India's second private conglomerate Birla, is very active in sectors such as sugar, cement, textile and mass-media. It showed a turnover of around $4.2 billion in 1996, officials said.
